preconditions: The attacker can issue SCRIPT DEBUG (SYNC mode) and EVAL to enter the synchronous Lua debugger (available to clients when ACL is not used to restrict it)
A debugger command longer than 1024 bytes, or one split by TCP framing across two connRead() calls
No authentication or special privilege is required in a default (ACL-less) deployment

evidence.vulnerable_version: valkey 9.1.3 (latest stable); the vulnerable readReadCommandInternal() is present at commit 41fb27b2 (parent of the fix) and unchanged in 9.1.3
evidence.fixed_version: 7dfa61e04390990da64b9e982c3b0fc0da8c7c82 (2026-10-31, PR #5127) — present in 9.2.0-rc2 but NOT backported to the 9.1.x stable line (9.1.3)
evidence.observed_result:
The faithful C model reproduces the exact readReadCommandInternal() flow: the entry assert serverAssert(*argc == 0), the parsing of the '*<count>
' header that sets *argc = count, and the keep_reading exit when a bulk argument's body has not fully arrived (which the vulnerable code reaches without resetting *argc). Driving a partial command "*3
$5
hel" (header complete, body incomplete) leaves *argc == 3; the retry re-enters readReadCommandInternal() and the assert fires — SIGABRT (exit 134) in the child, modelling the whole-server crash in SYNC mode. The fixed variant resets *argc = 0 on keep_reading and re-enters cleanly. Marker: VALKEY-RABBIT-CONFIRMED.

real_exploit.target: valkey src/scripting_engine.c::readReadCommandInternal() partial-read assert, as fixed by 7dfa61e0
real_exploit.backend: faithful C model of the assert + '*<count>\r\n' header parse + the keep_reading partial-body exit, run in a forked child so the vulnerable SIGABRT (serverAssert -> abort()) is observed and the fixed reset avoids it
real_exploit.demonstrated: a partial-read debugger command fires the *argc==0 assert and SIGABRTs the server process (vulnerable), while the *argc=0 reset prevents it (fixed); the commit message confirms the real server asserts in SYNC mode and exits with SIGABRT

evidence.notes: 0-day in the latest stable: no CVE/GHSA; the fix 7dfa61e0 ('Script debugger: reset *argc on partial-read exit to fix server crash in SYNC mode', PR #5127, Madelyn Olson) is in 9.2.0-rc2 but not backported to 9.1.3. CWE-617 (reachable assertion) / CWE-400 (DoS). Severity MEDIUM 5.9: AC:H reflects the need to enter the synchronous Lua debugger and split a command across reads, but the impact is a whole-server SIGABRT (A:H), not a per-client drop. The crash is in the server process (SYNC mode), so it takes down the entire valkey instance.
